title: Very Hot Drinks Could Increase Cancer Risk
paragraphs: There's nothing like a hot drink on a cold day. But if your drink is too hot, it could actually have bad repercussions for your health.
A study has found that regularly drinking very hot drinks could increase your risk of esophageal cancer. This type of cancer affects the esophagus, which connects the mouth and throat to the stomach.
Researchers from the University of Oxford looked at 14 years of data from nearly 1 million middle-aged men and women in the UK.
Participants were asked how they like to have their hot drinks — "warm," "hot" or "very hot."
The results showed that the hotter people like their drinks, the higher their risk of esophageal cancer is.

The risk was over three times higher among people who like their drinks "very hot" compared to people who like their drinks "warm." The risk was highest for people who have six or more cups of very hot drinks a day.
Part of the problem might be that people are too impatient.
According to the BBC, the temperature of tea made with water that has just been boiled will lower to about 90 or 95 degrees Celsius once it's poured into a cup.
And while adding milk helps lower that temperature, Keren Papier, one of the researchers, said it's still best to give your drink some time to cool down before drinking it.
Papier said previous research done in South America, where it's common to drink a hot drink called yerba mate, found a similar connection between hot drinks and esophageal cancer.

However, the researchers said the overall risk of developing esophageal cancer is still low, even for people who regularly have very hot drinks — and other factors like smoking and alcohol pose a greater risk for this type of cancer.
